turns.q: Is Supertech Supernova Astralis in Sector 94 on track for possession, and what is the risk if it slips?
turns.answer:
If you mean Astralis itself, it appears already delivered/ready-to-move rather than “on track for a future possession.” Multiple listings and the developer’s project page show Astralis possession around September 2020, with completion recorded in November 2022.
astralis.supertechnoida
+2

Astralis status

Supertech’s own project page lists Astralis possession as September 2020.
astralis.supertechnoida

Aggregator listings describe Astralis as ready to occupy / completed on 27 November 2022, with RERA registration UPRERAPRJ7263.
quikr

Resale listings for Astralis units also describe them as ready-to-move.
squareyards

So, for an Astralis buyer, the practical issue is usually obtaining/validating possession, occupation documentation, registration, and dues clearance, not waiting for construction completion.

Why the broader project is risky

The larger Supernova development in Sector 94 remains materially riskier because its developer SPV, Supertech Realtors Pvt Ltd (SRPL), entered corporate insolvency resolution proceedings after a default to Bank of Maharashtra. The NCLT appointed an interim resolution professional, and reporting at the time noted that buyers already in possession had less reason to worry, while those yet to receive possession could be affected.
hindustantimes

The unresolved risk is concentrated in the remaining under-construction tower, Spira, rather than Astralis: Supernova comprises Nova East, Nova West, Astralis (reported delivered) and Spira (under construction).
hindustantimes
+1

What happens if possession slips

If you are buying an Astralis resale unit, a delay in handover or registration is mainly a transaction/documentation risk. But if your purchase is tied to unfinished Supernova inventory or Spira, a slip could mean:

Construction and completion risk: insolvency can interrupt funding, contractor arrangements, approvals, and day-to-day project control.
hindustantimes

Approval-related risk: a Supreme Court-appointed panel reportedly required prior written approval for sales, transfers, assignments, conveyances, or creation of third-party rights in SRPL projects; unauthorised transactions were stated to be void and at the buyer’s own risk.
moneycontrol

Financial exposure: Supernova was reported to carry very large liabilities, and completion depended on resolution/financing arrangements; earlier reporting cited Kotak funding intended to clear bank dues and support completion.
timesofindia.indiatimes

Recovery uncertainty: even with insolvency protections, an allottee’s remedy may become a claim in the resolution process rather than a straightforward enforceable handover timeline.

Practical checks before paying

Confirm the exact tower, unit number, allotment letter, and seller’s title/authority—not merely “Supernova.”

For any resale or transfer in an SRPL project, obtain written approval from the court-appointed panel before payment; the notice reportedly makes unapproved transfers void.
moneycontrol

Verify current UP RERA status, completion/occupation certificate, outstanding dues, and encumbrance for the specific unit.

Prefer registered possession with keys, occupancy documentation, maintenance transfer, and no unresolved dues over a token possession letter.

If the unit is in Spira or another unfinished phase, treat the expected possession date as conditional on the insolvency resolution and funding plan.
hindustantimes
+1

Bottom line: Astralis is reported delivered, so it is not really “on track” for future possession. The material slippage risk applies to the wider Supernova project—especially Spira—where insolvency, approval requirements, and funding uncertainty could delay completion or complicate buyers’ rights.
hindustantimes
+2

turns.q: Can I trust Supertech as a builder? What happened with their delayed projects?
turns.answer:
I would not treat Supertech as a low-risk builder today. Its record includes large-scale, multi-year delays and insolvency proceedings; however, completion of many affected projects is now being handled by state-owned NBCC under court supervision, which reduces—but does not eliminate—delivery risk.
indianexpress
+1

What went wrong

Supertech left numerous projects in Noida, Greater Noida, Meerut and other locations stalled after buyers had paid most of the cost. In some projects, construction stopped around 2014–16, leaving buyers waiting for years and pursuing legal remedies.
indianexpress
+1

The company subsequently entered insolvency proceedings. In December 2024, the NCLAT directed NBCC to complete 16 of Supertech’s stalled projects, covering nearly 50,000 homes; the Supreme Court later upheld that mandate.
indianexpress
+1

Scale of the delays
Issue	Current position
Projects under NBCC completion plan	16 stalled Supertech projects across Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Karnataka. 
economictimes

Homes in those projects	About 50,962 units. 
economictimes

Units sold	About 39,870. 
economictimes

Units handed over	About 24,871. 
economictimes

Units still undelivered	About 14,999. 
economictimes

Funding for completion	NBCC has floated tenders worth about Rs 9,620 crore for construction and related work. 
economictimes
Is it safe to buy from Supertech now?

For an existing buyer in an NBCC-supervised project: the situation is more structured than before, because NBCC has a court-backed mandate and has begun tendering work. But buyers have still reported slow progress, and the proposed start of major construction/repair work has reportedly been pushed to January 2027.
economictimes.indiatimes
+1

For a new purchase from Supertech: I would be very cautious. The brand’s track record, insolvency history, and the fact that thousands of units remain undelivered make it a high-risk choice unless the specific project is demonstrably complete, registered, and ready for immediate possession/registration.
indianexpress
+1

For resale in a completed Supertech tower: risk depends more on the individual project’s completion certificate, occupancy certificate, registry status, maintenance, and encumbrances than on the builder’s name alone.

Practical checks before buying

Verify the exact project and tower—not just “Supertech”—on the UP RERA website.

Ask for the occupancy certificate, completion certificate, and confirm whether registry/possession is currently possible.

Check whether the project is among the 16 NBCC-supervised projects; if so, obtain the latest NCLAT/NBCC status and expected completion timeline.
indianexpress
+1

Prefer ready-to-move inventory with clear title and registration over under-construction or “near possession” inventory.

Speak with existing owners in the same tower about water, power, maintenance, pending dues, and actual registry experience.

Bottom line: Supertech’s delayed projects are real and severe, but there is now a court-monitored NBCC-led completion process for many of them. For a new purchase, treat Supertech as high risk; only consider a specific unit if it is legally complete and independently verifiable.
indianexpress

turns.q: For a 1.4 crore flat in Noida, what is the total cost including stamp duty, registration and GST?
turns.answer:
For a ₹1.40 crore flat in Noida, the total depends mainly on whether it is under construction (GST applies) or ready-to-move (no GST), and on the ownership structure. Stamp duty and registration are calculated on the higher of the agreement value or the applicable circle-rate value.
vidastu

Cost calculation
Scenario	Stamp duty	Registration	GST	Total cost
Male sole owner, under construction	7% = ₹9.80 lakh	1% = ₹1.40 lakh	5% = ₹7.00 lakh	₹1.582 crore
Male sole owner, ready-to-move	7% = ₹9.80 lakh	1% = ₹1.40 lakh	Nil	₹1.512 crore
Joint male + female, under construction	6.5% = ₹9.10 lakh	1% = ₹1.40 lakh	5% = ₹7.00 lakh	₹1.575 crore
Joint male + female, ready-to-move	6.5% = ₹9.10 lakh	1% = ₹1.40 lakh	Nil	₹1.505 crore

Noida’s standard stamp duty is 7%, registration is 1%, and GST on a non-affordable under-construction residential flat is 5% without input-tax credit.
vidastu
+2

Important caveats

The women’s 1% stamp-duty concession generally applies only up to ₹1 crore, so a ₹1.4 crore flat may not qualify for the reduced 6% rate; verify the current UP registration notification before relying on it.
prateekgroup
+1

If the circle rate for the flat’s project/location is higher than ₹1.4 crore, stamp duty and registration must be calculated on that higher value.
vidastu

GST is nil for a completed ready-to-move flat with a completion/occupation certificate and for resale of a completed property.

turns.q: If I take an 80% loan on a 1.5 crore flat, what is my EMI and how much cash do I need up front?
turns.answer:
For a ₹1.5 crore flat with an 80% home loan, your loan would be ₹1.20 crore and your minimum equity/down payment would be ₹30 lakh. At an illustrative 8% annual interest rate, the EMI is roughly ₹86,000–₹99,000 per month depending on tenure. HDFC lists an 8% starting rate for eligible borrowers, while SBI advertises home-loan rates from 7.50% p.a.; your actual rate will depend on credit profile, income, property, and lender.

You should also budget separately for purchase-related costs, which are not usually covered by the 80% loan:

Stamp duty and registration charges, commonly around 5–7% of property value depending on the state and buyer profile.

GST if applicable, typically for under-construction property.

Legal, valuation, processing, insurance, and interior/furnishing costs.

So, as a practical planning number, keep ₹30 lakh for the down payment plus roughly ₹8–12 lakh or more for taxes and charges, depending on your state and whether the flat is under construction. Lenders commonly finance around 80–90% of the property value, with the remainder funded by the buyer.
